title: The Arch and the Unfinished Theatre: Tamburini from the Marche to Buenos Aires
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Ascoli Piceno: the birth the register does not settle
stops.date_confidence: the day and the city are firm across every source reached; the year is not. es.wikipedia gives 1846, it.wikipedia's raw wikitext gives AnnoNascita = 1848 and its body says he was born at Ascoli Piceno in 1848, and the Istituto Italiano di Cultura di Córdoba prints 1848-1891 in the same text that bills its 29 January 2016 tribute as his 170th anniversary, a figure only 1846 supports. No civil or baptismal record was consulted. 1846 orders this file and settles nothing. An earlier draft's rival birthplace, Jesi, is dropped: Jesi is the home of his correspondent, not of his family
stops.campa: Ascoli Piceno stands in travertine where the Castellano runs into the Tronto, a papal town of towers around one broad stone square. On the twenty-ninth of January a son is born there, into a family the province will remember as Garibaldian in sympathy. He belongs to the last generation of Marchigiani born subjects of the Pope. The year is not settled: one register gives 1846 and another 1848, and the day and the city are the only things every account agrees on. The city keeps him eleven years, and then the family goes down to the coast.
suggested_refs: The historic centre of Ascoli Piceno, Piazza del Popolo and the travertine quarter

stops.name: Ancona: the family moves to the port
stops.date_confidence: it.wikipedia says the family moved to Ancona when he was eleven and gives no year; 1857 is derived from that age against the earlier of the two disputed birth years and is a placeholder. No month, no address. The coordinate is the Ancona city centre
stops.campa: The family moves to Ancona, the elbow of the Adriatic, where Trajan's arch stands out on the mole and the sea is the town's whole business. He is about eleven. He goes to the liceo and then to the technical institute, and he learns the harbour the way a boy learns a harbour, by the ships in it. Physics, chemistry, mechanics, drawing: the curriculum of a kingdom that is being assembled year by year and needs engineers more than it needs painters. He is very good at the drawing.
suggested_refs: The port of Ancona and the Arch of Trajan on the mole

stops.name: Istituto Tecnico Benincasa: the laboratory assistant
stops.date_confidence: attested by it.wikipedia, which names De Bosis and the physics and chemistry laboratory verbatim; an earlier draft downgraded this to unconfirmed tradition and added meteorological observation, which the source does not support. The year is a placeholder inside his schooling. The institute building was not located, so the coordinate duplicates the Ancona city point
stops.campa: At the Benincasa the naturalist Francesco De Bosis picks him out of the class and takes him on as assistant in the laboratory of physics and chemistry. It is the only apprenticeship he will ever have that is not architectural, and it prints itself on the way he works afterwards: he will measure cathedrals course by course and argue from dimensions in official memoranda. For now he is a boy among glass and balances, ruling instrument tables, keeping a cabinet in order.
suggested_refs: Istituto Tecnico Benincasa, Ancona; the scientific cabinet of Francesco De Bosis

stops.name: Bologna: the double title
stops.date_confidence: the 1872 degree is attested by es.wikipedia and corroborated by it.wikipedia; no month is given anywhere. The coordinate is the university's historic seat on Via Zamboni, not a faculty building
stops.campa: He goes to Bologna, to the oldest university in Europe, and comes out in 1872 an ingegnere-architetto. Engineer and architect in one title: in Italy a technical rank among many, and in Argentina eleven years later exactly the credential a government wants when it has decided to build its ministries in a hurry and cannot wait for an artist. He leaves the arcades with no building to his name and no permanent post. Ten years of provincial appointments follow the degree.
suggested_refs: The University of Bologna, faculty of engineering, degree of 1872

segments.name: Ten Years of Other Men's Buildings

stops.name: Urbino: architecture taught in the ducal city
stops.date_confidence: it.wikipedia lists the Urbino teaching post without years. The date is a placeholder inside the decade between the Bologna degree and the Argentine contract, and the coordinate is the city rather than any building of the university
stops.campa: He teaches architecture at Urbino, in the hill town where Federico da Montefeltro's palace sits on its own cliff and every student of the art in Italy must sooner or later reckon with that courtyard. The appointment is one of a chain: a season here, a season in another town, a salary that comes from a ministry and never from a client. He is a man of thirty instructing other people in an art nobody has yet paid him to practise. Which years he spends in the ducal city, no source records.
suggested_refs: The Palazzo Ducale of Urbino and its courtyard

stops.name: Duomo di Pisa: the cathedral measured
stops.date_confidence: the Pisa post at the Accademia delle belle arti and the cathedral surveys are attested by it.wikipedia, which says he published the resulting drawings, 'di notevole dettaglio e rifinitura'; an earlier draft denied any published outcome. The 1879 local newspaper notice of six large pen plates could not be fetched. The year is approximate within the Pisa appointment
stops.campa: Teaching architectural drawing at the Pisan academy, he takes the cathedral apart with a rule. Nobody has commissioned him to do it. Course by course of the striped marble, arcade by arcade of the west front, the whole eleventh-century fabric goes onto paper at a finish closer to engraving than to survey. It is the largest thing he has made so far and he has made it for himself, out of access to a scaffold and an appetite for other men's proportions. Then he publishes the plates.
suggested_refs: The Duomo of Pisa; Tamburini's published surveys, later studied by Stefano Santini

stops.name: Ancona: the portals of Giorgio Orsini
stops.date_confidence: it.wikipedia pairs these surveys with the Pisa campaign and gives no date; 1879 orders the segment. Neither San Francesco alle Scale nor Sant'Agostino was located to a coordinate, so the stop sits at the Ancona city point rather than at either church
stops.campa: Back in the port of his schooling he measures the two churches Giorgio Orsini of Sebenico left there, San Francesco alle Scale and Sant'Agostino. He draws them as he drew Pisa, without a commission and without a publisher waiting. Their portals are the strangest Gothic on this coast: Venetian in the carving, Dalmatian in the hand, stacked in tiers that stop where the money stopped. He works up from the threshold with the harbour at his back, counting the tiers off one at a time.
suggested_refs: San Francesco alle Scale and Sant'Agostino, Ancona, portals by Giorgio Orsini di Sebenico

stops.name: Naples: the ornament class
stops.date_confidence: attested by Claudia Shmidt, Seminario de Crítica 81 (IAA/FADU-UBA, 1997), p.9, who places him teaching ornament at the Accademia's school of architecture before he sailed and traces the doctrine to Giuseppe Pisanti in continuity with Errico Alvino. it.wikipedia does not list a Naples post at all; the year is a placeholder before 1883
stops.campa: In Naples he teaches ornament at the Accademia di Belle Arti, inside a school that argues one thing above all others: that past styles are to be brought up to date according to what the present needs, functionally and expressively, and not copied. Giuseppe Pisanti teaches it after Errico Alvino, and Tamburini teaches it after Pisanti. Every memorandum he will file in Buenos Aires about Gothic courts and modernised Greek libraries restates this lesson. He takes it aboard ship with him.
suggested_refs: The Scuola di Architettura of the Accademia di Belle Arti, Naples; the teaching of Errico Alvino and Giuseppe Pisanti
sources: Claudia Shmidt, 'Edificios públicos para una capital permanente', Seminario de Crítica 81, IAA/FADU-UBA, 1997, p.9

stops.name: Chiaravalle: the palazzina for Gustavo Marulli
stops.date_confidence: it.wikipedia's Chiaravalle article calls the building a palazzina raised at the end of the nineteenth century by Tamburini and now the town library of over 35,000 volumes; the 1881 date and the client's name come from the dossier and are not independently attested, and the 1907 municipal purchase rests on a local restoration report not fetched. The pool's coordinate missed the comune by about 7.4 km and is corrected here
stops.campa: In the flat sugar-beet country behind Ancona, the landowner Gustavo Marulli wants a house and hires him to draw it. It is the first time anyone pays him to build rather than to teach or to record. The palazzina goes up on the edge of Chiaravalle, a small correct thing in a small town, built at the end of the century for one family and outliving them. The comune buys it. The rooms fill up with the thirty-five thousand volumes of the public library, and the reading tables go in under his ceilings.
suggested_refs: The palazzina Marulli, Chiaravalle (Ancona), now the biblioteca comunale

stops.name: Ancona: the Palazzo Rheinold at the theatre square
stops.date_confidence: it.wikipedia gives the address, the corner of corso Garibaldi and piazza del Teatro, calls the building his probable first work, and places it in the Rome years up to 1883; no exact year exists, so 1882 orders the segment. The coordinate is the square of the Teatro delle Muse, correcting a pool value about 700 m away. The spelling varies as Rheinold, Reinold and Reinald across sources
stops.campa: On the corner where corso Garibaldi opens into the square of the Teatro delle Muse he puts up the Palazzo Rheinold, neo-Renaissance, the first substantial building anywhere that is his own from the ground. Ancona is filling in its new streets, and a private palazzo on a theatre square is the ordinary work of an ordinary provincial career. The year is nowhere recorded, and the client's name is spelled Rheinold, Reinold and Reinald in different hands. It faces a theatre.
suggested_refs: Palazzo Rheinold, corso Garibaldi at piazza del Teatro, Ancona

stops.name: Rome: the engineering school before the ocean
stops.date_confidence: it.wikipedia says he taught at the Scuola di Applicazione per gli Ingegneri in Rome until 1883. The coordinate is approximate: the school moved to Via Eudossiana only in the twentieth century, and no source consulted fixes its seat in his years
stops.campa: He takes a post at the school of application for engineers in Rome, the capital of a kingdom twelve years into holding it, and teaches men who will spend their lives on bridges and drains. Rome is where the appointments have been leading and where they stop. He is thirty-seven and has one palazzo, one country house and two campaigns of survey drawings behind him. In the same city, that year, the Argentine legation is under instruction to find an architect.
suggested_refs: The Scuola di Applicazione per gli Ingegneri, Rome

stops.name: Rome: the ambassador is told to hire an architect
stops.date_confidence: attested by Argentina.gob.ar and by Shmidt fn.12 after Alberto De Paula; both put the instruction at the beginning of 1883 and neither gives a day. Coordinate is the city
stops.campa: At the start of 1883 the government of Julio Argentino Roca instructs its ambassador in Rome to contract a professional to direct the architectural works of Buenos Aires. The republic has just taken the city away from the province and made it a federal capital, and a federal capital requires a face. What it wants is not one monument but a programme: ministries, courts, barracks, schools, an asylum for the immigrants coming off the ships. Argentina does not send for an architect. It sends for a department head.
suggested_refs: The Argentine legation in Rome, 1883; Alberto De Paula's reconstruction of the recruitment

stops.name: Rome: the first of July
stops.date_confidence: the date of the contract is attested by Shmidt fn.21 after De Paula and by Argentina.gob.ar; neither states where it was signed, and Rome is used here as the place of recruitment. The service that begins now is called seven years by Shmidt and six by Argentina's official profile, for the identical 1883-1890 span
stops.campa: He signs on the first of July as a specially engaged employee of the Departamento de Ingenieros Civiles. Not a competition and not a commission: a salaried post in a foreign state, with the whole public programme of a capital attached to it. He is a teacher of ornament with one palazzo to his name. Within seven years he will have drawn a government house, a court, a library, a police headquarters, a military hospital, normal schools in two cities, and the opera house.
suggested_refs: The contract of 1 July 1883 with the Departamento de Ingenieros Civiles

stops.name: Buenos Aires: the ship comes in
stops.date_confidence: February 1884 is Alberto De Paula's reconstruction, relayed by Shmidt fn.22; es.wikipedia gives only the year, and a late-1883 variant circulates. The coordinate is approximate: the 1880s anchorage and mole predate Puerto Madero by a decade
stops.campa: He comes ashore in February at a city with no proper port, lightered in from the roads like everyone else. While he was at sea the president wrote to Congress about the urgency of the government house, and the Chamber of Deputies spent a day in October debating a palace of justice, a police building, a military hospital, a school for schoolmistresses and an asylum for immigrants. Every item on that list is now his. He has never seen the city before.
suggested_refs: The pre-Puerto Madero anchorage of Buenos Aires; Diario de Sesiones de la Cámara de Diputados, session of 17 October 1883
sources: Shmidt, Seminario de Crítica 81, fn.15 and fn.22

stops.name: Buenos Aires: the desk Aberg leaves
stops.date_confidence: Shmidt records only that Aberg resigned soon after Tamburini's contract was concluded and gives no date; March 1884 orders the segment after the February arrival. The title Inspector General of Architectural Works comes from es.wikipedia. Coordinate is the shared Buenos Aires city pin, since the department's own seat is not fixed in the sources consulted
stops.campa: Enrique Aberg has been Director of Public Works and has a design on the table for the government house. Tamburini has been hired, in plain words, to revise it. Aberg resigns soon after the contract is concluded. The Italian takes the drawings, the office and the standing of Inspector General of architectural works for the nation, and finds the first job waiting is not a building but the joining of two. Whether the two men ever met, and what was said if they did, no source records.
suggested_refs: The Departamento de Ingenieros Civiles under the Ministerio del Interior, 1884

segments.name: The House That Was Two Houses

stops.name: Casa Rosada: the work he calls unpleasant
stops.date_confidence: the 1884 commission is attested by en.wikipedia's Casa Rosada article, which credits Tamburini, Aberg and Kihlberg and no one else; the month is a placeholder. The quotation is from his own Memorias, printed by Shmidt pp.7-8. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from the corpus pin for the Casa Rosada and Plaza de Mayo
stops.campa: On the east side of the Plaza de Mayo stand two buildings that have nothing to do with each other: Carl Kihlberg's post and telegraph office, finished five years ago, and what is left of the old government residence. He is ordered to make them one palace. He does not pretend to like it. In the report he files upward he writes that the thing had been projected using the old post office and part of the old residence, and that this made the work disagreeable and too complex.
stops.quote: el edificio se había proyectado utilizando la antigua casa de Correos y Telégrafos y parte de la antigua residencia del Gobierno, lo que hacía el trabajo desagradable y demasiado complejo
stops.quote_source: Tamburini, Memorias del Departamento de Obras Públicas de la Nación, quoted in Claudia Shmidt, Seminario de Crítica 81 (IAA/FADU-UBA, 1997), pp.7-8
suggested_refs: Carl Kihlberg's Palacio de Correos y Telégrafos, 1873-1879, absorbed into the Casa Rosada

stops.name: Casa Rosada: the styles that will not agree
stops.date_confidence: the quotation is from his Memorias as printed in Shmidt p.8 n.23, which carries in the same note his account of the Rivadavia front, given a grandiose aspect so far as the too limited height of the existing buildings allowed. No month or year attaches to the memorandum itself; 1885 orders the segment
stops.campa: He sets out, in writing, exactly what he is up against. German windows on the ground floor that will not sit with Renaissance columns or with Venetian and Florentine windows on the first, and above the whole quarrel a set of heavy German roofs. His solution is stated as flatly as the problem: he has tried to harmonise without binding himself to those parts. The sentence goes upward into an official report, under a heading about the union of the government buildings.
stops.quote: las ventanas germanas del piso bajo no armonizan con las columnas del Renacimiento o con ventanas venecianas o florentinas del primer piso, las cuales a su vez forman un extraño contraste con los pesados techos germanos que cubre el edificio. Por esto he tratado de armonizar sin ligarme con esas partes.
stops.quote_source: Tamburini, Memorias, quoted in Shmidt, Seminario de Crítica 81, p.8 n.23
suggested_refs: Tamburini's Memorias to the Director of Public Works on the union of the government buildings
sources: Shmidt, Seminario de Crítica 81, p.8 n.23

stops.name: Casa Rosada: the arch
stops.date_confidence: en.wikipedia's Casa Rosada article credits the great central archway to Tamburini and dates the design to 1884; the arch and the works around it run through the middle of the decade, and 1886 is a placeholder inside that span rather than a completion date. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from the corpus Casa Rosada pin
stops.campa: Between the two buildings he throws a single monumental arch, and at that moment they stop being two buildings. The design is dated 1884. Everything the republic does afterwards happens on the balcony above it or in the courtyard behind it: the speeches, the resignations, the crowds in the plaza looking up at one opening. The colour is not his, the wings are not his, and the post office underneath is Kihlberg's to the last cornice. The arch is his.
suggested_refs: The central archway of the Casa Rosada, joining the post office to the government house

stops.name: Plaza Lavalle: the palace of justice refused
stops.date_confidence: Shmidt p.8 dates the episode to 1884-1885 and records that Tamburini and the French engineer Norbert Maillart were the only two professionals invited by the Executive, and that the Congressional commission chose Maillart and faulted Tamburini's plan distribution and his handling of programmatic hierarchy. An earlier draft placed the episode in the late 1880s. The quotation is from his project presentation as printed in Shmidt p.9
stops.campa: Two men are invited to draw the nation's courts, and he is one of them. He proposes a building carrying the seal of the Middle Ages, and defends the choice not as novelty but as history: Vienna and Berlin and many cities of Italy and England, he writes, have chosen this style for the houses where judges sit. The Congressional commission reads his plans, faults the distribution and his handling of programmatic hierarchy, and gives the palace to the French engineer Norbert Maillart.
stops.quote: Viena, Berlín, muchas ciudades de Italia e Inglaterra al proyectar edificios que se destinan a residencia de los jueces, han elegido este estilo pero naturalmente variado según el carácter de la arquitectura de cada pueblo.
stops.quote_source: Tamburini, Memorias, Palacio de Justicia project presentation, quoted in Shmidt, Seminario de Crítica 81, p.9
suggested_refs: The Palacio de Justicia on Plaza Lavalle, built to Norbert Maillart's design

stops.name: Plaza Lorea: the library that stays on paper
stops.date_confidence: the project is described in his Memorias 1885-1888, p.39, quoted by Shmidt p.13; no single year exists for it and 1886 orders the segment inside that span. The coordinate is derived from Plaza Lorea and the old Cuartel de Bomberos site and is approximate; the building was never raised
stops.campa: On the site of the old fire barracks he lays out a national library, and explains himself in the report: he wanted the building to carry its ancient character, because the first greatness of the sciences comes down from Egypt and Greece. Then he refuses the archaeology. Neither the Parthenon nor the Greco-Roman monuments of Pompeii, he writes, could be adopted in our days. What he draws is a Greek modernised for modern convenience. The building is never begun.
stops.quote: ni el Partenón ni los monumentos griegos romanos de Pompeya y de la magna Grecia, podían adoptarse en nuestros días, y es evidente que el concepto artístico, debe responder también en lo que se refiere a la comodidad moderna.
stops.quote_source: Tamburini, Memorias 1885-1888, p.39, quoted in Shmidt, Seminario de Crítica 81, p.13
suggested_refs: The site of the Cuartel de Bomberos at Plaza Lorea, proposed seat of the Biblioteca Nacional

stops.name: Moreno 1550: the police headquarters taken over
stops.date_confidence: Shmidt p.16 gives the sequence: Buschiazzo's municipal scheme of 1884 for a Plaza Lorea site, the state's purchase of a site a few blocks south, the transfer of the job to the national department, and Tamburini's new project as the one actually built; fn.46 records that Buschiazzo finished the building after Tamburini's death. No month is given, and the coordinate is derived from the Moreno 1550 address
stops.campa: Juan Antonio Buschiazzo has already drawn this building once, for the municipality, on a Plaza Lorea site, in 1884, when he was public-works chief to the intendente Torcuato de Alvear. Then the state buys land a few blocks south and the commission crosses from the city to the nation, which is to say from Buschiazzo's desk to Tamburini's. He draws it again, and his is the one that gets built. The two of them will cross twice more, and Buschiazzo will finish this building after his death. The address is Moreno 1550.
suggested_refs: The Departamento Central de Policía, Moreno 1550, Buenos Aires
sources: Shmidt, Seminario de Crítica 81, p.16 and fn.46

stops.name: Avenida Callao: the normal school extended
stops.date_confidence: Shmidt fn.44 quotes his Memorias 1885-1888, p.55, on the extension of the Escuela Normal de Maestras; the work is a span inside 1885-1888 and 1887 orders it. The coordinate is derived from the Avenida Córdoba block opposite the future Palacio de Aguas Corrientes and is approximate
stops.campa: The school for schoolmistresses is four years old, built by the architect Bunge in Gothic, and it is already too small for the number of women the republic wants teaching. He extends it in the same Gothic, matching a style he did not choose, and lays gardens around it. In the report he claims only what he did: a plan forming in the whole a distribution convenient and suited to this nature of buildings. No argument about the Middle Ages this time. Just more classrooms.
stops.quote: se confeccionó un plan que forma en un todo una distribución cómoda y adecuada a esta naturaleza de edificios
stops.quote_source: Tamburini, Memorias 1885-1888, p.55, quoted in Shmidt, Seminario de Crítica 81, p.15
suggested_refs: The Escuela Normal de Maestras of Buenos Aires, built 1883 by Bunge and extended by Tamburini

stops.name: Plaza del Congreso: the competition he does not enter
stops.date_confidence: Law 2204 of 21 October 1887 calls the first competition for the Congress and Law 2461 of 5 July 1889 moves the site; Shmidt fn.35 records that he entered neither, having drafted an unofficial scheme earlier while the site was undecided. Her inventory files the Congress under projects and not works, which dissolves the apparent conflict between it.wikipedia listing it among his buildings and en.wikipedia crediting Meano. Meano's 1895 win is from es.wikipedia
stops.campa: He has already drawn a congress, unasked, while the government was still arguing about where to put one. Then the law comes calling for entries, and he does not enter. The law comes again two years later with a different site, and he does not enter that one either. The second law has moved the site itself. The building will be won in 1895 by Víctor Meano, at this moment a young draughtsman inside his own office. Why he stayed out of both competitions, no source records.
suggested_refs: Law 2204 of 21 October 1887 and Law 2461 of 5 July 1889; the Palacio del Congreso by Víctor Meano

stops.name: Rosario: the normal school in the river port
stops.date_confidence: Shmidt's inventory lists the Escuela Normal de Maestras of Rosario among built works and gives no year; 1888 orders the segment. No address survives in any source reached, so the coordinate is the city centre and stands for an unlocated site
stops.campa: The office is national, so the drawings go up the river as well. In Rosario, the grain port that is becoming the country's second city, another normal school for schoolmistresses goes up to his department's design. The republic needs several thousand teachers who do not yet exist, Law 1420 having just made primary schooling free, secular and obligatory. No address for the school survives in anything reached. Rosario had no cathedral and wanted classrooms.
suggested_refs: The Escuela Normal de Maestras of Rosario
sources: Shmidt, Seminario de Crítica 81, project and works inventory

stops.name: Pozos y Caseros: the hospital in pavilions
stops.date_confidence: Shmidt fn.47 dates the design and construction to 1889, gives the street corner, and describes the Tollet pavilion system with a two-storey central administrative block flanked by symmetrical single-storey pavilions. The coordinate is derived from the corner of Pozos and Caseros and is approximate. The modern Hospital Militar Central in Palermo is a twentieth-century relocation and is not this building; an earlier draft's shared attribution with Aberg is dropped
stops.campa: At Pozos and Caseros he lays out the central military hospital on the Tollet system: a two-storey administrative block in the middle and single-storey pavilions to either side, matched, separated, so that air moves between them and the wards do not breathe on one another. The system is French and the plan follows it exactly, down to the spacing that keeps one ward's air out of the next. It is projected and built inside the single year 1889, faster than anything else he puts up in this country.
suggested_refs: The Hospital Militar Central at Pozos y Caseros, Buenos Aires, on Tollet's pavilion system

stops.name: Córdoba: the provincial government house enlarged
stops.date_confidence: Shmidt's inventory dates the project for the enlargement and reform of the Casa de Gobierno of Córdoba to 1886 and gives no month. The coordinate is the government house in the old colonial centre
stops.campa: Córdoba sends for him too. The province wants its government house made larger and made modern, and the national department lends out the Italian who is already reworking the one in Buenos Aires. Córdoba is the older capital, a university town of colonial cloisters that has decided to look like a European city in a decade. The project for the enlargement and reform is dated 1886. The province's bank, its opera house and its teaching hospital all come after it.
suggested_refs: The Casa de Gobierno of the province of Córdoba
sources: Shmidt, Seminario de Crítica 81, project and works inventory

stops.name: Calle Ancha: the horseshoe of the Teatro Rivera Indarte
stops.date_confidence: the 1887 design date, the construction by José Franceschi and the original name are attested by muva-faud-unc.org and es.wikipedia, which also gives the inauguration, 26 April 1891. The coordinate is from es.wikipedia and corrects a pool value about 500 m off. The recurrent local claim that the facade copies the San Carlo of Naples is carried by no source reached and is left out
stops.campa: Ramón J. Cárcano puts the idea to Governor Ambrosio Olmos, and Olmos hands it to Tamburini: an opera house for Córdoba, on the Calle Ancha. He draws a horseshoe auditorium in the Italian manner, tier on tier, with the Paris Opéra somewhere behind the stair, and José Franceschi builds it. Nothing he does in Buenos Aires will be finished in his lifetime. This one is. It opens on the twenty-sixth of April 1891 under the name of Rivera Indarte, and no source places him in the hall that night.
suggested_refs: The Teatro Rivera Indarte, now Teatro del Libertador General San Martín, Avenida Vélez Sarsfield, Córdoba
sources: es.wikipedia, 'Teatro del Libertador General San Martín'

stops.name: Córdoba: the bank inaugurated in May
stops.date_confidence: the inauguration of 17 May 1889, the two-year construction under the technical direction of the engineer José Franceschi, and the plasterwork by Arturo Nembrini Gonzaga are attested by the bank's own institutional page. Two coordinates for the building circulate about 40 m apart; the one used here is used again for the museum stop below
stops.campa: The Banco Provincial goes up in two years under the technical direction of the engineer José Franceschi and opens on the seventeenth of May 1889. It is among the first buildings in South America drawn from the start for a financial house rather than adapted into one. He is drawing the province a market at San Vicente in the same years, on his own account and not the state's. Inside, a stained-glass ceiling stands over the central hall, and the plasterwork is by Arturo Nembrini Gonzaga, in a manner the bank itself compares to Versailles.
suggested_refs: The Banco de la Provincia de Córdoba, inaugurated 17 May 1889

stops.name: Barrio Alberdi: the hospital of the clinics
stops.date_confidence: es.wikipedia names Tamburini as designer of the original building of the Hospital Nacional de Clínicas at Santa Rosa 1564; Shmidt describes the commission passing to the national department after the province rejected local proposals, and the pavilion type sited away from the built-up city, but her fn.49 records that according to the Registro Oficial the author would be the Ingeniero Camici-Roncoroni. The contradiction is not resolved here. No month; the hospital opened only on 24 May 1913
stops.campa: The province cannot settle on a design for its teaching hospital, so the file goes to the national department and comes back with pavilions: wards set well beyond the built-up city, on open ground, spaced for air, in the same logic as the military hospital at Pozos y Caseros. He notes himself that the ornamental treatment has come out sumptuous. It takes twenty-four years to open. Two names stand in the record as its author, his and an Ingeniero Camici-Roncoroni's, and which is right nothing reached will say.
suggested_refs: The Hospital Nacional de Clínicas, Santa Rosa 1564, Barrio Alberdi, Córdoba

stops.name: 25 de Mayo 551: a house for the President
stops.date_confidence: Shmidt's inventory of his private works lists the Juárez Celman residence at 25 de Mayo 551 and Avenida Leandro N. Alem 546 without a year; 1889 orders it inside the president's term. The coordinate is derived from the street address and is approximate. The rural estate La Elisa at Capitán Sarmiento is a dossier claim not carried here
stops.campa: Miguel Juárez Celman is Roca's brother-in-law and Roca's successor, and he wants a house in the city. Tamburini draws it, on his own account and not the department's. The distinction matters to him: after six years of drawing for a ministry, this is a client and a fee that belongs to him. The house stands on the corner of 25 de Mayo and what is now Avenida Leandro N. Alem, and the inventory that lists it gives no year at all. The same list of private work carries a bank and a market in Córdoba.
suggested_refs: The Juárez Celman residence, 25 de Mayo 551 / Av. Leandro N. Alem 546, Buenos Aires
sources: Shmidt, Seminario de Crítica 81, inventory of private works

stops.name: Plaza Lavalle: the theatre moved across the city
stops.date_confidence: Argentina.gob.ar dates the Colón project to 1887; Shmidt attributes the removal of the old theatre from the Plaza de Mayo to an initiative of intendente Torcuato de Alvear and identifies the old house as the work of the engineer Enrique Pellegrini. Her fn.25 records the three buildings Tamburini projected for this one square. The 1889 concession to the impresario Angelo Ferrari, carried by an earlier draft, is not in the source it was attributed to and is dropped. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from the corpus Teatro Colón pin
stops.campa: The old Colón stands north of the government house, facing the Plaza de Mayo, built by the engineer Enrique Pellegrini, and Torcuato de Alvear wants it off his plaza. So the opera house moves to Plaza Lavalle, across the city, onto the square where the artillery park stands, and Tamburini draws it. That makes three separate buildings he has projected for this one square: the courts that went to Maillart, a museum of Argentine products at Libertad and Lavalle, and this one. Only the third is ever begun.
suggested_refs: The old Teatro Colón of Enrique Pellegrini on the Plaza de Mayo; Shmidt fn.25 on the three Tamburini projects for Plaza Lavalle

stops.name: Buenos Aires: he leaves the state
stops.date_confidence: Shmidt says he resigned his post as an employee of the national state after seven years of intense activity, and that the Colón was a commission he had almost won in advance; Argentina's official profile calls the same service six years. No exact date exists in either source, and January 1890 orders the segment
stops.campa: He resigns. Seven years of drawing whatever the republic asked for, government house, courts, library, barracks, hospitals, schools, and he walks out of the department to practise on his own with the opera house in hand. He is in his forties, at the top of the profession, in a country that is about to run out of money. One account of the service calls it seven years and another calls it six, for the identical span, and no exact date of leaving exists in either.
suggested_refs: Tamburini's resignation from the Departamento de Ingenieros Civiles

stops.name: Teatro Colón: the first stone
stops.date_confidence: 25 May 1890 is the date given by the theatre's own institutional history, which also records the original target for completion, 12 October 1892, chosen for the fourth centenary of Columbus. en.wikipedia elsewhere gives 1889 loosely for the start of construction; the specific institutional date is preferred here and the looser one recorded. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from the corpus Teatro Colón pin
stops.campa: On the twenty-fifth of May, the national holiday, they lay the cornerstone at Plaza Lavalle, on the square where the artillery park stands. The house is to be finished on the twelfth of October 1892, four hundred years to the day from the first landfall. The calculation behind that date is that a country which has just paid for a capital can pay for an opera house as well. It opens in 1908, eighteen years late, under the third architect to hold the drawings.
suggested_refs: The cornerstone of the Teatro Colón, 25 May 1890

stops.name: Teatro Colón: the artillery park across the street
stops.date_confidence: the rising of 26-29 July 1890 took the Parque de Artillería, on the ground of today's Plaza Lavalle, which es.wikipedia notes stood facing the newly begun works of the Teatro Colón. Tamburini's own presence is attested nowhere, so the stop sits at his building site and not at the park; an earlier draft placed the rising in Parque Tres de Febrero, 4.5 km away. His financial ruin in the crisis is stated directly by it.wikipedia
stops.campa: Two months after the stone, Leandro Alem's armed civic regiment takes the artillery park, and the artillery park stands directly across from the works. From the twenty-sixth to the twenty-ninth of July there is fighting in the streets around the foundation trench. The president falls, the currency collapses, and the money that was to pay for the opera house evaporates along with everything Tamburini has put by. Work at Plaza Lavalle stops. The trench stays open.
suggested_refs: The Parque de Artillería, site of the Revolución del Parque, 26-29 July 1890, facing the Colón works

stops.name: Buenos Aires: the letter to the marchese Colocci
stops.date_confidence: the wording is carried verbatim by it.wikipedia, which names the correspondent as the marchese Colocci of Jesi and cites Fabio Mariano, 'Francesco Tamburini', in L'età dell'eclettismo (Nerbini, Firenze, 2004), a study not fetched. The date and the place of writing are inferences from the crisis year and are not attested; an earlier draft truncated the sentence and the full form is used here
stops.campa: He writes home to Italy, to his friend the marchese Adriano Colocci of Jesi. The country he came to build is in receivership, the works at Plaza Lavalle are stopped, his savings are gone, and he has no state salary behind him any more. What he sends back across the Atlantic is not an account of losses, and it asks for nothing. Four clauses, and the last of them is a sailor's phrase out of the Adriatic port where he grew up, thirty years and one ocean away: vento alle vele.
stops.quote: E fede ci vuole! Torneranno tempi migliori, si rifarà qualche cosa, e allora... vento alle vele!
stops.quote_source: Tamburini to the marchese Adriano Colocci of Jesi, 1890, quoted in it.wikipedia after Fabio Mariano, 'Francesco Tamburini', in L'età dell'eclettismo (Nerbini, Firenze, 2004)
suggested_refs: The Colocci correspondence, cited by Fabio Mariano in L'età dell'eclettismo (2004)

stops.name: Buenos Aires: the death and the tribute
stops.date_confidence: the year is contradicted across sources: es.wikipedia's infobox gives 1890 while that article's own category files him under Fallecidos en 1891; teatrocolon.org.ar says he died in 1891; the Istituto Italiano di Cultura di Córdoba prints 1848-1891. No primary record was reached, no month or day is recorded anywhere, and no burial record, cemetery listing or grave marker could be located: a Find A Grave search returned no accessible result and both Wikipedias end the life without mentioning interment. 1891-01-01 orders the file and decides nothing. His Córdoba theatre opened on 26 April 1891 and no source places him there. Meano's tribute is undated
stops.campa: He dies in Buenos Aires with the opera house at foundation level and the country still in the wreck of the crash. Víctor Meano, who came into his office as a young man and now inherits the drawings, says in public what the profession will spend the next century arguing about: that to him alone belongs the merit of the general idea of the project. Where they buried him is not recorded in anything that can now be read, in Argentina or in the Marche.
stops.quote: a él solo pertenece el mérito de la idea general del proyecto
stops.quote_source: Víctor Meano on Tamburini, quoted in Gustavo Brandariz, 'El Colón de Francesco Tamburini', in Teatro Colón: puesta en valor y actualización tecnológica (GCBA/FADU-UBA), p.37
suggested_refs: Meano's public tribute to Tamburini after his death, printed in Brandariz's study of the Colón
sources: Gustavo Brandariz, 'El Colón de Francesco Tamburini', p.37

stops.name: Buenos Aires: the report printed after him
stops.date_confidence: the report titled 'Teatro Colón' appears in Memoria del Departamento de Obras Públicas de la Nación 1889-1891, t.3, pp.59-76, Buenos Aires 1892, and is cited as a primary source by Signos Históricos (UAM-Iztapalapa), article view/538; no month. The coordinate is the Casa Rosada pin, standing for the seat of the national administration, since the department's own address is not fixed in the sources consulted
stops.campa: The department publishes its memoir for the years 1889 to 1891, and eighteen pages of it are his: the technical report on the Teatro Colón, filed before he died and printed after. It is the fullest statement of what the building was meant to be, written by the only person who knew, and it goes into a government volume almost nobody reads. Historians arguing a century later about whose theatre the Colón is cite volume three, pages fifty-nine to seventy-six.
suggested_refs: Francisco Tamburini, 'Teatro Colón', Memoria del Departamento de Obras Públicas de la Nación 1889-1891, t.3, pp.59-76 (1892)

stops.name: Ascoli Piceno: the city remembers him
stops.date_confidence: it.wikipedia says the city of Ascoli dedicated a series of commemorations and celebrations to him in 1892; it does not say what they consisted of, and no month is given. The coordinate is the same city point used for the birth
stops.campa: Two years after he dies six thousand miles away, the town of towers holds a season of commemorations and celebrations for him. Ascoli Piceno had him for eleven years at the beginning and claims him back at the end, on the strength of a government house, a bank and an opera house in a country most of the province could not have found on a map. What the commemorations consisted of, a plaque or a ceremony in the square or a printed tribute, went unrecorded even there.
suggested_refs: The 1892 commemorations at Ascoli Piceno

stops.name: Teatro Colón: the campaign to pull it down
stops.date_confidence: Shmidt dates Buschiazzo's demolition campaign to the end of 1899 and gives no day; November orders it. The municipal inspection commission she quotes next is introduced with 'años después' and is therefore carried in the following stop, not here. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from the corpus Teatro Colón pin
stops.campa: The theatre has stood half-built for five years, out of money since 1894, an unroofed shell on the best square in the city with weeds in the boxes. At the end of 1899 Juan Antonio Buschiazzo leads a campaign to have it demolished outright: wrong on aesthetic grounds, wrong for the square, better cleared than completed. It is the third time the work of the two men has crossed, and the first time Tamburini is not there to answer. The walls stay up.
suggested_refs: Buschiazzo's campaign of late 1899 for the demolition of the unfinished Colón

stops.name: Teatro Colón: the inspection commission's verdict
stops.date_confidence: the commission is undated in Shmidt, who introduces it with 'años después' of the 1899 campaign; Telémaco Susini printed its words in Arquitectura N.6, July 1904, p.59, so the commission falls between those bounds and 1903 is a placeholder inside them. An earlier draft dated it to 1899 and named the periodical 'Revista Arquitectura'; both are corrected. The words reach this file at two removes, Shmidt quoting Susini quoting the commission
stops.campa: A municipal inspection commission goes through the building and reports that the project is at odds with every rule of aesthetics. Then it goes further, and puts the charge in the language of public money: this is an official building costing several millions, and it should therefore be a model theatre, whereas in its origin it was nothing but the product of an enterprise of profit and speculation, with almost no account taken of the safety of the audience.
stops.quote: el teatro Colón... debe ser un teatro modelo porque es un edificio público, oficial, que cuesta varios millones [y en cambio] no ha sido otra cosa en su origen que el producto de una empresa de lucro y de especulación en que poco se ha tenido absolutamente en cuenta la seguridad de los concurrentes
stops.quote_source: Municipal inspection commission report, quoted by Telémaco Susini, 'Defectos del nuevo edificio del Teatro Colón', Arquitectura N.6, July 1904, p.59, as cited in Shmidt, Seminario de Crítica 81, p.18
suggested_refs: Telémaco Susini, 'Defectos del nuevo edificio del Teatro Colón', Arquitectura N.6, July 1904
sources: Shmidt, Seminario de Crítica 81, p.18 and fn.53-54

stops.name: Teatro Colón: opened with Aida
stops.date_confidence: the 1894 financial stall, Meano's murder in 1904, the engagement of the Belgian Jules Dormal and the opening of 25 May 1908 with Verdi's Aida are all from the theatre's own institutional history, which also records that areas such as the Salón Dorado were still unfinished at the opening. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from the corpus Teatro Colón pin
stops.campa: Eighteen years to the day after the cornerstone, on the same national holiday, the house opens with Aida sung by an Italian company. Meano carried the work after Tamburini and was murdered in 1904; Jules Dormal carried it after Meano and gave it a changed structure and a heavier French finish. Two of the three architects named on the building are dead by the opening. Parts of the house, the Salón Dorado among them, are still unfinished on the night.
suggested_refs: The inauguration of the Teatro Colón, 25 May 1908

stops.name: Archivo General de la Nación: the watercolour scanned
stops.date_confidence: the Wikimedia Commons file page records the December 2006 scan of a watercolour of Tamburini's original project for the Teatro Colón held by the Archivo General de la Nación, and its release as a public-domain image; the drawing itself is undated beyond having been made before his death. The coordinate is the Archivo's building
stops.campa: In the Archivo General de la Nación there is a watercolour of the theatre as he first drew it, undated beyond having been made before he died, before Meano modified it and Dormal modified it again: elevation, wash, the house he argued for. The building on that paper does not exist and never did, and it is the only place his Colón can now be looked at. In December 2006 somebody lays the sheet on a flatbed scanner and releases the file to the public domain.
suggested_refs: Wikimedia Commons, File:Teatro Colón (Francesco Tamburini).jpg, from the Archivo General de la Nación
sources: Wikimedia Commons file page, 'Teatro Colón (Francesco Tamburini).jpg'

stops.name: Córdoba: the bank keeps his name
stops.date_confidence: the Istituto Italiano di Cultura di Córdoba dates its public tribute and the inauguration of the museum space to 29 January 2016, while the bank's own institutional page dates the naming of the Museo Arquitecto Francisco Tamburini to 2009. Whether 2016 was a re-inauguration, an expansion, or a misdescription is not resolved. Coordinate as in the 1889 stop for the same building
stops.campa: The bank he drew in Córdoba still counts money, and inside it there is a museum with his name over the door. On the twenty-ninth of January, the day he was born, the Italian cultural institute and the provincial bank hold a tribute under the stained-glass ceiling of the hall he designed. The bank dates the naming of the museum to 2009 and the institute dates it to 2016. Of everything he built on two continents, this is the building that carries his name.
suggested_refs: The Museo Arquitecto Francisco Tamburini inside the Banco de la Provincia de Córdoba
